description: Registered calls admit one schema-lifecycle job and return its job_id/status before declaration parsing or lifecycle effects. Logical uninstall — marks every ownership row for the namespace inactive while leaving tables and data on disk. Reversible via install_plugin_schema (which reactivates and applies any new diff). To actually drop the data, call purge_plugin_schema after.
embedding_description: Queue the complete schema lifecycle operation and read its exact job for the final outcome. Mark a plugin's installed schema inactive without dropping tables or losing data. Logical uninstall: marks every ownership row for the namespace inactive while tables + data stay on disk. Reversible via install_plugin_schema (reactivates + applies any new diff). To actually drop data, call purge_plugin_schema after. Returns status (uninstalled / not_installed).

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Queued ActionResult receipt with data.job_id and data.status; the exact job.result retains the complete original lifecycle response and job.error its typed failure.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Admission confirms the job was persisted, not that the schema changed. Read service_interface::job_service::get_job by this exact id until terminal before using lifecycle status, tables or force results.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Poll the exact job id. Preserve the existing force and ownership premises. Reconcile an uncertain outcome or lost volatile declaration without replaying schema effects.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Marks the plugin-schema ownership rows inactive for the namespace. Tables and data on disk are not touched — uninstall is intentionally reversible.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: Most failures are connectivity or transactional issues at the Postgres layer; the lifecycle itself does not raise on a not-yet-installed namespace (returns status='not_installed').
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For Postgres connectivity errors: confirm postgres_state_management_plugin is healthy. The transaction rolls back atomically on failure.
